name: Expanded LANL temporal GRU event predictor
limitations: Unusual event sequences are not proof of malware; no attack labels or malware performance evaluation.
Expanded bounded2015 LANL enterprise host/network prefix; Windows application/session domain still differs.
Only process start/end, DNS and network destination-port categories influence scores. File, Registry and process-access evidence is excluded.
LANL process names are anonymized, with no PID/parent IDs; router flow records have no process attribution. Process ancestry is displayed evidence, not learned by this model.
Scores are anomaly surprise in nats, not confidence percentages or probabilities of maliciousness.
Validation selected99th-percentile maximum surprise across8 targets/24-event windows. Session alerts cannot be interpreted as a calibrated false-positive rate.
Mirror publisher documents official-source byte-identical acquisition; official-source full-file equality is not independently verified.
Missing telemetry changes observed sequences and may change scores; low scores do not establish safety.

Training aggregates host-wide events; a watched process session is a narrower stream. DNS-port and other rare token groups have very limited support despite the expanded data. Unknown NetFlow destination ports are common and differ from direct Windows observations.
training_dataset: LANL2015 expanded32MiB pinned proc/flows/dns prefixes; original-v1 time region excluded.
selection: Minimum validation next-event NLL across fixed two capacities/two seeds; each epoch selected with patience3 and minimum improvement0.0001. Threshold99th-percentile maximum of8 targetNLLs. Test not used.
